Box plots: the big picture
A box plot shows the center and spread of a data distribution using five numbers.
Five-number summary
From left to right: minimum, first quartile, median, third quartile, maximum.
The number line
Read positions from the number-line scale, not from the visual width of the screen.
The box
The left edge is Q1, the right edge is Q3. The box contains the middle fifty percent.
The median
The line inside the box is the median, not necessarily the mean.
Whiskers
In a basic box plot, the whiskers extend from the box to the minimum and maximum.
Worked example
For two, five, nine, thirteen, sixteen: the median is nine, and the box spans five through thirteen.
Interquartile range
Subtract Q1 from Q3. Thirteen minus five equals eight.
Overall range
Subtract minimum from maximum. Sixteen minus two equals fourteen.
Comparing plots
A box with a larger IQR shows more spread among the middle half, when the scales match.
Shifting scores
Adding five to every score moves the plot five units right without changing its spread.
Scaling scores
Multiplying every value by three triples the range, IQR, and whisker lengths.
Possible outliers
An upper outlier fence equals Q3 plus one point five times IQR. A modified box plot may display outliers separately.
